23: impl Command for External {
24:     fn name(&self) -> &str {
25:         "run-external"
26:     }
27: 
28:     fn usage(&self) -> &str {
29:         "Runs external command."
30:     }
31: 
32:     fn signature(&self) -> nu_protocol::Signature {
33:         Signature::build(self.name())
34:             .input_output_types(vec![(Type::Any, Type::Any)])
35:             .required("command", SyntaxShape::String, "External command to run.")
36:             .rest("args", SyntaxShape::Any, "Arguments for external command.")
37:             .category(Category::System)
38:     }
39: 
40:     fn run(
41:         &self,
42:         engine_state: &EngineState,
43:         stack: &mut Stack,
44:         call: &Call,
45:         input: PipelineData,
46:     ) -> Result<PipelineData, ShellError> {
47:         let cwd = engine_state.cwd(Some(stack))?;
48: 
49:         // Find the absolute path to the executable. On Windows, set the
50:         // executable to "cmd.exe" if it's is a CMD internal command. If the
51:         // command is not found, display a helpful error message.
52:         let name: Spanned<String> = call.req(engine_state, stack, 0)?;
53:         let executable = if cfg!(windows) && is_cmd_internal_command(&name.item) {
54:             PathBuf::from("cmd.exe")
55:         } else {
56:             let paths = nu_engine::env::path_str(engine_state, stack, call.head)?;
57:             let Some(executable) = which(&name.item, &paths, &cwd) else {
58:                 return Err(command_not_found(
59:                     &name.item,
60:                     call.head,
61:                     engine_state,
62:                     stack,
63:                 ));
64:             };
65:             executable
66:         };
67: 
68:         // Create the command.
69:         let mut command = std::process::Command::new(executable);
70: 
71:         // Configure PWD.
72:         command.current_dir(cwd);
73: 
74:         // Configure environment variables.
75:         let envs = env_to_strings(engine_state, stack)?;
76:         command.env_clear();
77:         command.envs(envs);
78: 
79:         // Configure args.
80:         let args = eval_arguments_from_call(engine_state, stack, call)?;
81:         #[cfg(windows)]
82:         if is_cmd_internal_command(&name.item) {
83:             use std::os::windows::process::CommandExt;
84: 
85:             // The /D flag disables execution of AutoRun commands from registry.
86:             // The /C flag followed by a command name instructs CMD to execute
87:             // that command and quit.
88:             command.args(["/D", "/C", &name.item]);
89:             for arg in &args {
90:                 command.raw_arg(escape_cmd_argument(arg)?.as_ref());
91:             }
92:         } else {
93:             command.args(args.into_iter().map(|s| s.item));
94:         }
95:         #[cfg(not(windows))]
96:         command.args(args.into_iter().map(|s| s.item));
97: 
98:         // Configure stdout and stderr. If both are set to `OutDest::Pipe`,
99:         // we'll setup a pipe that merge two streams into one.
100:         let stdout = stack.stdout();
101:         let stderr = stack.stderr();
102:         let merged_stream = if matches!(stdout, OutDest::Pipe) && matches!(stderr, OutDest::Pipe) {
103:             let (reader, writer) = os_pipe::pipe()?;
104:             command.stdout(writer.try_clone()?);
105:             command.stderr(writer);
106:             Some(reader)
107:         } else {
108:             command.stdout(Stdio::try_from(stdout)?);
109:             command.stderr(Stdio::try_from(stderr)?);
110:             None
111:         };
112: 
113:         // Configure stdin. We'll try connecting input to the child process
114:         // directly. If that's not possible, we'll setup a pipe and spawn a
115:         // thread to copy data into the child process.
116:         let data_to_copy_into_stdin = match input {
117:             PipelineData::ByteStream(stream, metadata) => match stream.into_stdio() {
118:                 Ok(stdin) => {
119:                     command.stdin(stdin);
120:                     None
121:                 }
122:                 Err(stream) => {
123:                     command.stdin(Stdio::piped());
124:                     Some(PipelineData::ByteStream(stream, metadata))
125:                 }
126:             },
127:             PipelineData::Empty => {
128:                 command.stdin(Stdio::inherit());
129:                 None
130:             }
131:             value => {
132:                 command.stdin(Stdio::piped());
133:                 Some(value)
134:             }
135:         };
136: 
137:         // Spawn the child process. On Unix, also put the child process to
138:         // foreground if we're in an interactive session.
139:         #[cfg(windows)]
140:         let mut child = ForegroundChild::spawn(command)?;
141:         #[cfg(unix)]
142:         let mut child = ForegroundChild::spawn(
143:             command,
144:             engine_state.is_interactive,
145:             &engine_state.pipeline_externals_state,
146:         )?;
147: 
148:         // If we need to copy data into the child process, do it now.
149:         if let Some(data) = data_to_copy_into_stdin {
150:             let stdin = child.as_mut().stdin.take().expect("stdin is piped");
151:             let engine_state = engine_state.clone();
152:             let stack = stack.clone();
153:             thread::Builder::new()
154:                 .name("external stdin worker".into())
155:                 .spawn(move || {
156:                     let _ = write_pipeline_data(engine_state, stack, data, stdin);
157:                 })
158:                 .err_span(call.head)?;
159:         }
160: 
161:         // Wrap the output into a `PipelineData::ByteStream`.
162:         let child = ChildProcess::new(
163:             child,
164:             merged_stream,
165:             matches!(stderr, OutDest::Pipe),
166:             call.head,
167:         )?;
168:         Ok(PipelineData::ByteStream(
169:             ByteStream::child(child, call.head),
170:             None,
171:         ))
172:     }

195: /// Removes surrounding quotes from a string. Doesn't remove quotes from raw
196: /// strings. Returns the original string if it doesn't have matching quotes.
197: fn remove_quotes(s: &str) -> &str {
198:     let quoted_by_double_quotes = s.len() >= 2 && s.starts_with('"') && s.ends_with('"');
199:     let quoted_by_single_quotes = s.len() >= 2 && s.starts_with('\'') && s.ends_with('\'');
200:     let quoted_by_backticks = s.len() >= 2 && s.starts_with('`') && s.ends_with('`');
201:     if quoted_by_double_quotes || quoted_by_single_quotes || quoted_by_backticks {
202:         &s[1..s.len() - 1]
203:     } else {
204:         s
205:     }
206: }

208: /// Evaluate all arguments from a call, performing expansions when necessary.
209: pub fn eval_arguments_from_call(
210:     engine_state: &EngineState,
211:     stack: &mut Stack,
212:     call: &Call,
213: ) -> Result<Vec<Spanned<String>>, ShellError> {
214:     let cwd = engine_state.cwd(Some(stack))?;
215:     let mut args: Vec<Spanned<String>> = vec![];
216:     for (expr, spread) in call.rest_iter(1) {
217:         if is_bare_string(expr) {
218:             // If `expr` is a bare string, perform tilde-expansion,
219:             // glob-expansion, and inner-quotes-removal, in that order.
220:             for arg in eval_argument(engine_state, stack, expr, spread)? {
221:                 let tilde_expanded = expand_tilde(&arg);
222:                 for glob_expanded in expand_glob(&tilde_expanded, &cwd, expr.span)? {
223:                     let inner_quotes_removed = remove_inner_quotes(&glob_expanded);
224:                     args.push(inner_quotes_removed.into_owned().into_spanned(expr.span));
225:                 }
226:             }
227:         } else {
228:             for arg in eval_argument(engine_state, stack, expr, spread)? {
229:                 args.push(arg.into_spanned(expr.span));
230:             }
231:         }
232:     }
233:     Ok(args)
234: }
235: 
236: /// Evaluates an expression, coercing the values to strings.
237: ///
238: /// Note: The parser currently has a special hack that retains surrounding
239: /// quotes for string literals in `Expression`, so that we can decide whether
240: /// the expression is considered a bare string. The hack doesn't affect string
241: /// literals within lists or records. This function will remove the quotes
242: /// before evaluating the expression.
243: fn eval_argument(
244:     engine_state: &EngineState,
245:     stack: &mut Stack,
246:     expr: &Expression,
247:     spread: bool,
248: ) -> Result<Vec<String>, ShellError> {
249:     // Remove quotes from string literals.
250:     let mut expr = expr.clone();
251:     if let Expr::String(s) = &expr.expr {
252:         expr.expr = Expr::String(remove_quotes(s).into());
253:     }
254: 
255:     let eval = get_eval_expression(engine_state);
256:     match eval(engine_state, stack, &expr)? {
257:         Value::List { vals, .. } => {
258:             if spread {
259:                 vals.into_iter()
260:                     .map(|val| val.coerce_into_string())
261:                     .collect()
262:             } else {
263:                 Err(ShellError::CannotPassListToExternal {
264:                     arg: String::from_utf8_lossy(engine_state.get_span_contents(expr.span)).into(),
265:                     span: expr.span,
266:                 })
267:             }
268:         }
269:         value => {
270:             if spread {
271:                 Err(ShellError::CannotSpreadAsList { span: expr.span })
272:             } else {
273:                 Ok(vec![value.coerce_into_string()?])
274:             }
275:         }
276:     }
277: }
278: 
279: /// Returns whether an expression is considered a bare string.
280: ///
281: /// Bare strings are defined as string literals that are either unquoted or
282: /// quoted by backticks. Raw strings or string interpolations don't count.
283: fn is_bare_string(expr: &Expression) -> bool {
284:     let Expr::String(s) = &expr.expr else {
285:         return false;
286:     };
287:     let quoted_by_double_quotes = s.len() >= 2 && s.starts_with('"') && s.ends_with('"');
288:     let quoted_by_single_quotes = s.len() >= 2 && s.starts_with('\'') && s.ends_with('\'');
289:     !quoted_by_double_quotes && !quoted_by_single_quotes
290: }

292: /// Performs tilde expansion on `arg`. Returns the original string if `arg`
293: /// doesn't start with tilde.
294: fn expand_tilde(arg: &str) -> String {
295:     nu_path::expand_tilde(arg).to_string_lossy().to_string()
296: }
297: 
298: /// Performs glob expansion on `arg`. If the expansion found no matches or the pattern
299: /// is not a valid glob, then this returns the original string as the expansion result.
300: ///
301: /// Note: This matches the default behavior of Bash, but is known to be
302: /// error-prone. We might want to change this behavior in the future.
303: fn expand_glob(arg: &str, cwd: &Path, span: Span) -> Result<Vec<String>, ShellError> {
304:     let Ok(paths) = nu_glob::glob_with_parent(arg, nu_glob::MatchOptions::default(), cwd) else {
305:         return Ok(vec![arg.into()]);
306:     };
307: 
308:     let mut result = vec![];
309:     for path in paths {
310:         let path = path.map_err(|err| ShellError::IOErrorSpanned {
311:             msg: format!("{}: {:?}", err.path().display(), err.error()),
312:             span,
313:         })?;
314:         // Strip PWD from the resulting paths if possible.
315:         let path_stripped = path.strip_prefix(cwd).unwrap_or(&path);
316:         let path_string = path_stripped.to_string_lossy().to_string();
317:         result.push(path_string);
318:     }
319: 
320:     if result.is_empty() {
321:         result.push(arg.to_string());
322:     }
323: 
324:     Ok(result)
325: }
326: 
327: /// Transforms `--option="value"` into `--option=value`. `value` can be quoted
328: /// with double quotes, single quotes, or backticks. Only removes the outermost
329: /// pair of quotes after the equal sign.
330: fn remove_inner_quotes(arg: &str) -> Cow<'_, str> {
331:     // Check that `arg` is a long option.
332:     if !arg.starts_with("--") {
333:         return Cow::Borrowed(arg);
334:     }
335:     // Split `arg` on the first `=`.
336:     let Some((option, value)) = arg.split_once('=') else {
337:         return Cow::Borrowed(arg);
338:     };
339:     // Check that `option` doesn't contain quotes.
340:     if option.contains('"') || option.contains('\'') || option.contains('`') {
341:         return Cow::Borrowed(arg);
342:     }
343:     // Remove the outermost pair of quotes from `value`.
344:     let value = remove_quotes(value);
345:     Cow::Owned(format!("{option}={value}"))
346: }
347: 
348: /// Write `PipelineData` into `writer`. If `PipelineData` is not binary, it is
349: /// first rendered using the `table` command.
350: ///
351: /// Note: Avoid using this function when piping data from an external command to
352: /// another external command, because it copies data unnecessarily. Instead,
353: /// extract the pipe from the `PipelineData::ByteStream` of the first command
354: /// and hand it to the second command directly.
355: fn write_pipeline_data(
356:     mut engine_state: EngineState,
357:     mut stack: Stack,
358:     data: PipelineData,
359:     mut writer: impl Write,
360: ) -> Result<(), ShellError> {
361:     if let PipelineData::ByteStream(stream, ..) = data {
362:         stream.write_to(writer)?;
363:     } else if let PipelineData::Value(Value::Binary { val, .. }, ..) = data {
364:         writer.write_all(&val)?;
365:     } else {
366:         stack.start_capture();
367: 
368:         // Turn off color as we pass data through
369:         Arc::make_mut(&mut engine_state.config).use_ansi_coloring = false;
370: 
371:         // Invoke the `table` command.
372:         let output =
373:             crate::Table.run(&engine_state, &mut stack, &Call::new(Span::unknown()), data)?;
374: 
375:         // Write the output.
376:         for value in output {
377:             let bytes = value.coerce_into_binary()?;
378:             writer.write_all(&bytes)?;
379:         }
380:     }
381:     Ok(())
382: }

384: /// Returns a helpful error message given an invalid command name,
385: pub fn command_not_found(
386:     name: &str,
387:     span: Span,
388:     engine_state: &EngineState,
389:     stack: &mut Stack,
390: ) -> ShellError {
391:     // Run the `command_not_found` hook if there is one.
392:     if let Some(hook) = &engine_state.config.hooks.command_not_found {
393:         let mut stack = stack.start_capture();
394:         // Set a special environment variable to avoid infinite loops when the
395:         // `command_not_found` hook triggers itself.
396:         let canary = "ENTERED_COMMAND_NOT_FOUND";
397:         if stack.has_env_var(engine_state, canary) {
398:             return ShellError::ExternalCommand {
399:                 label: format!(
400:                     "Command {name} not found while running the `command_not_found` hook"
401:                 ),
402:                 help: "Make sure the `command_not_found` hook itself does not use unknown commands"
403:                     .into(),
404:                 span,
405:             };
406:         }
407:         stack.add_env_var(canary.into(), Value::bool(true, Span::unknown()));
408: 
409:         let output = eval_hook(
410:             &mut engine_state.clone(),
411:             &mut stack,
412:             None,
413:             vec![("cmd_name".into(), Value::string(name, span))],
414:             hook,
415:             "command_not_found",
416:         );
417: 
418:         // Remove the special environment variable that we just set.
419:         stack.remove_env_var(engine_state, canary);
420: 
421:         match output {
422:             Ok(PipelineData::Value(Value::String { val, .. }, ..)) => {
423:                 return ShellError::ExternalCommand {
424:                     label: format!("Command `{name}` not found"),
425:                     help: val,
426:                     span,
427:                 };
428:             }
429:             Err(err) => {
430:                 return err;
431:             }
432:             _ => {
433:                 // The hook did not return a string, so ignore it.
434:             }
435:         }
436:     }
437: 
438:     // If the name is one of the removed commands, recommend a replacement.
439:     if let Some(replacement) = crate::removed_commands().get(&name.to_lowercase()) {
440:         return ShellError::RemovedCommand {
441:             removed: name.to_lowercase(),
442:             replacement: replacement.clone(),
443:             span,
444:         };
445:     }
446: 
447:     // The command might be from another module. Try to find it.
448:     if let Some(module) = engine_state.which_module_has_decl(name.as_bytes(), &[]) {
449:         let module = String::from_utf8_lossy(module);
450:         // Is the command already imported?
451:         let full_name = format!("{module} {name}");
452:         if engine_state.find_decl(full_name.as_bytes(), &[]).is_some() {
453:             return ShellError::ExternalCommand {
454:                 label: format!("Command `{name}` not found"),
455:                 help: format!("Did you mean `{full_name}`?"),
456:                 span,
457:             };
458:         } else {
459:             return ShellError::ExternalCommand {
460:                 label: format!("Command `{name}` not found"),
461:                 help: format!("A command with that name exists in module `{module}`. Try importing it with `use`"),
462:                 span,
463:             };
464:         }
465:     }
466: 
467:     // Try to match the name with the search terms of existing commands.
468:     let signatures = engine_state.get_signatures(false);
469:     if let Some(sig) = signatures.iter().find(|sig| {
470:         sig.search_terms
471:             .iter()
472:             .any(|term| term.to_folded_case() == name.to_folded_case())
473:     }) {
474:         return ShellError::ExternalCommand {
475:             label: format!("Command `{name}` not found"),
476:             help: format!("Did you mean `{}`?", sig.name),
477:             span,
478:         };
479:     }
480: 
481:     // Try a fuzzy search on the names of all existing commands.
482:     if let Some(cmd) = did_you_mean(signatures.iter().map(|sig| &sig.name), name) {
483:         // The user is invoking an external command with the same name as a
484:         // built-in command. Remind them of this.
485:         if cmd == name {
486:             return ShellError::ExternalCommand {
487:                 label: format!("Command `{name}` not found"),
488:                 help: "There is a built-in command with the same name".into(),
489:                 span,
490:             };
491:         }
492:         return ShellError::ExternalCommand {
493:             label: format!("Command `{name}` not found"),
494:             help: format!("Did you mean `{cmd}`?"),
495:             span,
496:         };
497:     }
498: 
499:     // We found nothing useful. Give up and return a generic error message.
500:     ShellError::ExternalCommand {
501:         label: format!("Command `{name}` not found"),
502:         help: format!("`{name}` is neither a Nushell built-in or a known external command"),
503:         span,
504:     }
505: }

507: /// Searches for the absolute path of an executable by name. `.bat` and `.cmd`
508: /// files are recognized as executables on Windows.
509: ///
510: /// This is a wrapper around `which::which_in()` except that, on Windows, it
511: /// also searches the current directory before any PATH entries.
512: ///
513: /// Note: the `which.rs` crate always uses PATHEXT from the environment. As
514: /// such, changing PATHEXT within Nushell doesn't work without updating the
515: /// actual environment of the Nushell process.
516: pub fn which(name: &str, paths: &str, cwd: &Path) -> Option<PathBuf> {
517:     #[cfg(windows)]
518:     let paths = format!("{};{}", cwd.display(), paths);
519:     which::which_in(name, Some(paths), cwd).ok()
520: }
521: 
522: /// Returns true if `name` is a (somewhat useful) CMD internal command. The full
523: /// list can be found at https://ss64.com/nt/syntax-internal.html
524: fn is_cmd_internal_command(name: &str) -> bool {
525:     const COMMANDS: &[&str] = &[
526:         "ASSOC", "CLS", "ECHO", "FTYPE", "MKLINK", "PAUSE", "START", "VER", "VOL",
527:     ];
528:     COMMANDS.iter().any(|cmd| cmd.eq_ignore_ascii_case(name))
529: }
530: 
531: /// Returns true if a string contains CMD special characters.
532: #[cfg(windows)]
533: fn has_cmd_special_character(s: &str) -> bool {
534:     const SPECIAL_CHARS: &[char] = &['<', '>', '&', '|', '^'];
535:     SPECIAL_CHARS.iter().any(|c| s.contains(*c))
536: }
537: 
538: /// Escape an argument for CMD internal commands. The result can be safely
539: /// passed to `raw_arg()`.
540: #[cfg(windows)]
541: fn escape_cmd_argument(arg: &Spanned<String>) -> Result<Cow<'_, str>, ShellError> {
542:     let Spanned { item: arg, span } = arg;
543:     if arg.contains('"') {
544:         // If `arg` is already quoted by double quotes, confirm there's no
545:         // embedded double quotes, then leave it as is.
546:         if arg.chars().filter(|c| *c == '"').count() == 2
547:             && arg.starts_with('"')
548:             && arg.ends_with('"')
549:         {
550:             Ok(Cow::Borrowed(arg))
551:         } else {
552:             Err(ShellError::ExternalCommand {
553:                 label: "Arguments to CMD internal commands cannot contain embedded double quotes"
554:                     .into(),
555:                 help: "CMD doesn't support escaping double quotes inside double quotes".into(),
556:                 span: *span,
557:             })
558:         }
559:     } else if arg.contains(' ') || has_cmd_special_character(arg) {
560:         // If `arg` contains space or special characters, quote the entire argument by double quotes.
561:         Ok(Cow::Owned(format!("\"{arg}\"")))
562:     } else {
563:         Ok(Cow::Borrowed(arg))
564:     }
565: }

567: #[cfg(test)]
568: mod test {
569:     use super::*;
570:     use nu_protocol::ast::ListItem;
571: 
572:     #[test]
573:     fn test_remove_quotes() {
574:         assert_eq!(remove_quotes(r#""#), r#""#);
575:         assert_eq!(remove_quotes(r#"'"#), r#"'"#);
576:         assert_eq!(remove_quotes(r#"''"#), r#""#);
